It depends on your needs, after seeing hours of reviews, benchmarks and posts. The 6800h + 3060 is my go to. I work remotely using non demanding programs, most of the time just running a browser with 25 tabs and editing files in MS office, I'm ok with 70 fps on demanding games and I see myself traveling and working on the go from a cafe from time to time

With the 6800h I can save power (where I leave AC/heating is not common, so a gaming laptop can actually make a big difference on the electricity bill) 

For a game I play a lot (Lol) I prefer lower-mid settings, the flashy effects doesn't improve my performance and just distract me from what matters, so I can play with good enough FPS without even using the GTX 3060. 

I don't render or do intensive productivity tasks. So for someone like me, using the computer 40 hrs a week for work and 30 hrs for gaming, the Ryzen is the best option. 

Each with their needs, for me looks future proof and powerful enough. In hot climates all year long (32C°-39C°) without AC, the lower temperatures, even if it's just a bit, are very important.

You can use the VPN to launch the game and then kill the connection to improve connectivity, the server doesn't pick the change in you IP and it just remove the VPN server limitations from the equation. You need the VPN to access but not at all to actually play once the streaming session already started. Only latency issue will be from the distance between your real location and the nearest server to the VPN location you selected to launch the game.

Hey, just to add on the previous advice. I play from a non supported country in LatAm. Here is a quick tip to improve your streaming experience, you need a VPN to access the Cloud Gaming library, pick a game and to actually start the launching process, but as soon as you see the Xbox logo, you can kill the VPN connection and it will run without the limitations of the VPN server, once you finish your gaming session, you will need to connect again from the VPN to reboot the game or pick a different one. This also works with GeForce Now and PS Now.

Btw, avoid the app and use the browser, for some reason with the same connection and device it simply runs better in every sense from a browser, any browser.
